newsitem.title: GERMANY: No point in Iran dialogue for now - Bonn politician.
newsitem.headline: No point in Iran dialogue for now - Bonn politician.

text.p: The chairman of the German parliament's foreign affairs committee said on Monday there was no point in resuming the policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran for the foreseeable future.

Karl-Heinz Hornhues also said a "high degree of joint action" by the West, especially the European Union, was important after last Thursday's ruling by a German court that Iranian leaders, including the state president and the religious leader, ordered the killing of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.

All EU nations except Greece have recalled their top diplomats from Tehran for consultation and the entire 15-nation bloc has suspended its "critical dialogue". Hornhues said a resumption of this policy appeared unwise.

"The problem is that the same people who were implicated in the Mykonos trial represent the Iranian leadership for the foreseeable future," Hornhues, a member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats, told Saar Radio.
The "critical dialogue" policy aimed to keep communication channels open to encourage more pro-Western elements in Iran while not losing sight of human rights.

Hornhues said the EU must now put pressure on Iran to change its ways. "I hope total isolation of Iran will create such strong pressure that Iran will reach a turning point in its politics for egotistical reasons," he said.
But Hornhues expressed scepticism about Washington's hardline policy of cutting off all ties to Iran and imposing trade sanctions. Hornhues said he did not favour going as far as the United States.

Last Thursday's verdict marked the first time a European court had clearly attributed political responsibility for any of the dozens of assassinations of Iranian opposition figures abroad since the Islamic revolution in 1979.
The verdict has provoked outrage in Iran, where hundreds of thousands of protesters rallied outside the German embassy on Sunday chanting anti-Western slogans.
